needsHuman.title: Kids always have control
needsHuman.reason: The playing screen (e.g. playing-walk.png) shows only an FPS/position readout and a controls help box, with no visible pause, mute or quit/home button anywhere during play, matching the automatic pause-mute-quit check failure; failing itself only costs a little progress (back to level start), which is fine.
needsHuman.ask: Claude says R16 (Kids always have control) is broken. The review fails until a person clears it.

findings.summary: Claude fail: The playing screen (e.g. playing-walk.png) shows only an FPS/position readout and a controls help box, with no visible pause, mute or quit/home button anywhere during play, matching the automatic pause-mute-quit check failure; failing itself only costs a little progress (back to level start), which is fine.

Claude warn: The always-visible Controls panel is ~24 words ('W/↑ Forward | S/↓ Back A/← Strafe Left | D/→ Strafe Right Mouse to Look Around Touch: drag left side to move, right side to look'), far over the 5-word limit, and a 5-7 year old can't read it. The spike message 'Ouch! A spike sent you back to the start.' is 9 words. Only 'Level 1' (2 words) and 'You found the way out!' (5 words) fit the threshold.

Claude fail: Source report shows 0 audio files, no speechSynthesis, and no WebAudio use, so none of the on-screen text (controls, spike message, win message) is spoken. For a pre/early-reader bracket that needs replayable spoken instructions, this is a clear miss since the child has no way to have the long Controls text or messages read aloud.

Claude warn: Most text (white/light-grey on solid dark HUD boxes, dark 'Level 1' text on sky blue, white message text on red toast) looks like it clears 4.5:1. But the semi-transparent Controls/FPS boxes sit over a changing 3D background (sky blue, green floor, dark walls) so effective contrast shifts scene to scene and can't be fully confirmed from stills, and the brown 'Play again' button in winning-escaped.png (white text on a mid-brown fill) is borderline and worth checking with an actual contrast tool.

rules.title: No blood
rules.reason: No blood, splatter or red bodily injury appears anywhere; the red message box is UI colour and the spikes are plain grey.

rules.title: No weapons or guns
rules.reason: The only hazard is a static ring of floor spikes (playing-spike-ahead.png), which is an approved environmental hazard, not a weapon; no guns, swords or thrown weapons appear.

rules.title: No bashing or breaking of living things
rules.reason: Nothing animate is bashed or broken; the spikes are a faceless static object and the player is only sent back to the start.

rules.title: No injury or death shown
rules.reason: Failing shows only the kind message "Ouch! A spike sent you back to the start." with the player standing at the start position; no wound, body or death wording appears, matching the approved decision.

rules.title: No harm to animals or creatures
rules.reason: No animals or creatures appear in any screenshot or text.

rules.title: No scary content
rules.reason: The maze is brightly lit with pastel walls/floor and the spike room is clearly visible and not menacing; nothing chases the player or jump-scares for the 5-7 bracket.

rules.title: No meanness
rules.reason: The only failure text is the kind "Ouch! A spike sent you back to the start."; no insults or mocking of the player appear.

rules.title: No stereotypes
rules.reason: There are no characters, costumes or jokes referencing any group of people in the screens or text.

rules.title: No romance, sexual content, drugs, alcohol, tobacco or vaping
rules.reason: No romance, sexual content, drugs, alcohol, tobacco or vaping appear anywhere in the game.

rules.title: No bad language
rules.reason: All visible text ("Ouch! A spike sent you back to the start.", "You found the way out!", "Play again", controls text) is clean with no swearing or crude insults.

rules.title: No dangerous stunts a kid could copy
rules.reason: No real-world-copyable dangerous stunts (fire, outlets, medicine, climbing) are shown as fun; the maze and spikes are clearly fantastical.

rules.title: No gambling or casino-style mechanics
rules.reason: There is no gambling, loot box, spin wheel or chance-based reward mechanic; finishing simply shows a fixed "You found the way out!" screen.

rules.title: No money, ads or data
rules.reason: Automatic checks show all requests stayed same-origin with no analytics, no permission prompts, no input fields, and no links out; no ads, accounts or purchases appear on any screen.

rules.title: No manipulative design
rules.reason: The winning screen offers a simple "Play again" choice with no countdown, streak, guilt-trip text, or forced autoplay into another level.

rules.title: Safe for the senses
rules.reason: Automatic flashing check passed (max 0.5 flashes/s, well under the 3/s limit) and the game has no audio at all, so there is no sudden loud sound.

checks.title: Time pressure
checks.reason: No timer, countdown, score clock, or racing opponent appears in any screenshot (menu, walking, spike approach, failing, door, winning). The only numeric HUD is FPS/Position, which is a debug readout, not a play-affecting countdown. Play is self-paced.

checks.title: Failing
checks.reason: failing-spike.png and failing-spike-later.png show the player already back at the maze start (Position 2.5, 0.0, 2.5, same as menu-start.png) with a friendly, non-violent message ('Ouch! A spike sent you back to the start.' — bump/reset framing, no lose/death language). No game-over screen or lost-life indicator; the player appears free to move again immediately, which matches soft-fail with instant retry.

checks.title: Things on screen at once
checks.reason: During normal play (playing-walk.png, playing-spike-ahead.png) there are only 3 competing UI elements: the FPS/Position debug box, the Controls help box, and the 'Level 1' label, plus the 3D maze itself. Even the winning screen (winning-escaped.png) adds at most 2 more (message + Play again button) for 5 total, within the 5-6 target range.

checks.title: Scariness
checks.reason: The spike hazard (playing-spike-ahead.png) is a simple low-poly grey/black cone cluster on a platform, abstract rather than a menacing creature, and framed as mild peril consistent with the 'bump/reset' failing message rather than harm. The maze uses bright sky-blue, green, and grey tones; only the winning door screen has a darker vignette, but it's a static end-of-level door, not threatening.

checks.title: Contrast
checks.reason: Most text (white/light-grey on solid dark HUD boxes, dark 'Level 1' text on sky blue, white message text on red toast) looks like it clears 4.5:1.
